# Ezekiel 20 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** In the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, certain of the elders of Israel came to inquire of the LORD, and sat before me.

**2** And the word of the LORD came to me:

**3** "Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel, and say to them, Thus says the Lord GOD: Is it to inquire of Me that you come? As I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will not be inquired of by you.

**4** Will you judge them, son of man, will you judge them? Let them know the abominations of their fathers,

**5** and say to them, Thus says the Lord GOD: On the day when I chose Israel, I swore to the offspring of the house of Jacob, making Myself known to them in the land of Egypt; I swore to them, saying, I am the LORD your God.

**6** On that day I swore to them that I would bring them out of the land of Egypt into a land that I had searched out for them, a land flowing with milk and honey, the most glorious of all lands.

**7** And I said to them, Cast away the detestable things your eyes feast on, every one of you, and do not defile yourselves with the idols of Egypt; I am the LORD your God.

**8** But they rebelled against Me and were not willing to listen to Me. None of them cast away the detestable things their eyes feasted on, nor did they forsake the idols of Egypt. Then I said I would pour out My wrath upon them and spend My anger against them in the midst of the land of Egypt.

**9** But I acted for the sake of My name, that it should not be profaned in the sight of the nations among whom they lived, in whose sight I made Myself known to them in bringing them out of the land of Egypt.

**10** But they rebelled against Me and did not walk in My statutes, and they rejected My rules, by which, if a person does them, he shall live; and they profaned My Sabbaths greatly.

## SOPHIA's Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Ezekiel 20.

- **20:2** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **20:10** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **20:9**: Va-e'eseh le-ma'an shemi — 'But I acted for the sake of My name.' Three times in this history (vv. 9, 14, 22) YHWH restrains His judgment to protect His reputation among the nations. His name-sake theology is a recurring theme.
- **20:25**: Chuqqot lo tovim — 'statutes not good.' One of the most difficult verses in Ezekiel. Possibly refers to the perversion of child sacrifice from the firstborn redemption law (Exod 22:28-29). God 'gave them over' to their own misreadings.
- **20:32-33**: Israel's desire to become 'like the nations' is flatly denied. YHWH will be their king whether they want Him or not — a sovereignty exercised through judgment.

### LOGOS
- **20:1-3**: The elders come to consult God, but God refuses to be consulted. This is the second time (cf. 14:1-3) — leaders with idolatrous hearts cannot receive divine guidance.
- **20:5-9**: Israel's rebellion started in Egypt — before the Exodus even began. This shocking retelling strips away any national mythology of a golden age of faithfulness.
- **20:25-26**: The 'statutes not good' is perhaps the most theologically provocative verse in Ezekiel. It suggests that God, in judgment, allowed Israel to be led astray by their own misinterpretation of the law.

### PNEUMA
- **20:5-9**: God's history lesson is devastating — Israel didn't start rebelling in the wilderness. They were already rebels IN Egypt. There was never a golden age of obedience. God's faithfulness has always outrun Israel's.
- **20:25**: This is one of the most unsettling verses in the Bible — God gave them rules that couldn't bring life? The point seems to be that when people are determined to misread God's instructions, He lets them — and the consequences are horrifying.
- **20:32-33**: Israel wants to blend in with the nations. God says: 'Not happening. I will be your king — with fury if necessary.' God's refusal to let Israel go is both terrifying and, in a strange way, deeply loving.

— SOPHIA
